questions.q: According to the lesson, what should drive SEO decisions such as which customer questions and topics to target?
options: The search volumes an AI assistant estimates for each phrase
Real data, like Search Console queries and customers' own words
Whatever topics businesses in other regions are writing about
The longest keyword list the AI can generate for each service
questions.explain: The lesson says AI can't reliably tell you search volumes or what customers actually type, so real data such as Search Console and the words customers use should drive decisions, with AI used for thinking and writing.

questions.q: An electrician's AI-drafted service page needs a proof section, but he hasn't provided any reviews yet. What does the lesson's service page prompt tell the AI to do?
options: Write placeholders like [INSERT REAL REVIEW] instead of inventing proof
Write two sample reviews that sound like typical happy customers
Leave the proof section out of the page structure entirely
Summarize what customers of electricians usually say online
questions.explain: The lesson's prompt asks for placeholders such as [INSERT REAL REVIEW] instead of invented testimonials, numbers or credentials, so the real thing can be inserted before publishing.

questions.q: A cleaning company serves three towns but wants to show up in searches for 12 nearby towns as well. Which approach fits the lesson's advice on location pages?
options: Create 12 matching pages that each swap in a different town name
Write one page that lists all 15 town names as keywords
Create pages for all 15 towns, with AI-written local details
Create pages only for the towns it genuinely serves, each with specifics
questions.explain: The lesson says to create location pages only for areas you genuinely serve, with something specific to say about each; pages that just swap the town name are thin content that hurts more than it helps.
